papers.title: Trust in Machine Learning-Aided Docking: A Systematic Review of Good Practices for Chemically Reliable Predictions
papers.abstract: The massive growth of chemical libraries presents both an opportunity and a challenge in large-scale virtual screening. Machine learning (ML) algorithms have successfully accelerated this process with surrogate docking models that learn patterns between molecular representations and docking scores for ranking undocked molecules. Deep learning (DL), which represents the majority of ML-boosted docking approaches, has a sophisticated capability of finding nonlinear, complex relationships in voluminous data. However, DL algorithms operate as black boxes, face difficulties in generalization and raise concerns on whether correct predictions are, in fact, made for causal relationships between chemical structure and biological activity. Candidate molecules cannot be confidently tested if predictions are not understandable in human terms. The lack of understanding of relevant chemical properties impairs compound discovery, optimization and novelty, reinforcing the high-risk and high-cost scenario of drug design. To offer insights for expanding the recent breakthroughs achieved with the docking/ML integration, this review included 57 ML-aided docking papers from January 2020 to August 2026. We assessed how ML predictions are generated, refined and chemically interpreted to reliably reduce docking simulations and ideally increase experimental hit rates by data-driven and expert-driven decisions on compound selection. On this matter, the proper implementation of eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques is informative to elucidate if and how trustworthy are predicted hits from a chemical perspective, assuring a safer and more effective decision-making process for finding true hits. Nonetheless, only four (7.0%) out of 57 papers applied XAI techniques, mostly involving feature attribution methods, but not the state-of-the-art contrastive explanations method. Therefore, the implementation of XAI in ML-boosted docking is still scarce and needs formalization to avoid misinterpreting results. We review the various opportunities and limitations for integrating ML-aided docking with XAI techniques alongside complementary trust-enhancing strategies present in the included studies, such as sampling strategies, target diversity, ensemble and consensus docking, active learning, ensemble models, physicochemical and pharmacophore-based filtering, multiobjective optimization of molecular properties, confidence metrics of predefined acceptable errors, and expected model improvement along iterations. Given the broad applications of XAI across scientific domains and proof-of-concept studies in computational chemistry, we believe benchmarking and combining current and novel trust-enhancing strategies in ML-aided docking can go beyond finding initial hits. It supports both the statistical assessment including XAI in predictions and the mechanistic understanding of chemically relevant drug candidates for transparent and credible model and drug development.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该综述讨论ML代理模型加速分子对接及可解释性，与FEA代理建模的采样效率、UQ和约束优化仅有概念层面的间接关联。
llm.why_not_core: It addresses surrogate docking for drug discovery with no FEA, no solid mechanics, no implant/biomechanics design, and no uncertainty quantification of a physics simulation.

summary_zh.motivation: 大规模虚拟筛选需要可信的机器学习代理对接模型。
summary_zh.method: 系统综述2020至2026年间57篇ML辅助对接文献，评估预测生成、精化与化学解释流程。
summary_zh.result: 仅7%研究使用可解释AI，采样策略、集成与多目标优化等信任增强手段仍待规范化。
summary_zh.validation: 文献计量与定性综述，无实验或数值验证。

summary_en.motivation: Surrogate docking models are needed to screen massive chemical libraries, yet their black-box nature undermines trust in predicted hits.
summary_en.method: A systematic review of 57 ML-aided docking studies published between 2020 and 2026, assessing how predictions are generated, refined, and chemically interpreted.
summary_en.result: Only 7% of studies employed explainable AI, while trust-enhancing strategies such as sampling, ensembling, active learning, and multi-objective filtering remain inconsistently formalized.
summary_en.validation: Qualitative literature synthesis without experimental or numerical benchmarking.
